programmes.network_quality: Medium to high for German startups going international
programmes.location_requirement: You need to be based in Germany. A German legal entity is described as beneficial but not required - EXIST-funded startups still forming a GmbH are explicitly welcome to apply.

programmes.notes: Notable because it is one of very few programmes in this lane that says in its own words that a legal entity is not required to apply, explicitly welcoming pre-GmbH applicants. The binding condition is instead residence - based in Germany. Two deadlines fall within seventeen days of this sweep, so this is time-critical if the residence test can be met or negotiated. Short three-day formats, so brand value is modest.

programmes.name: Antler ONE Residency (Continental Europe)
programmes.region: Germany (Berlin hub), with launch pads in Munich and Amsterdam
programmes.page_evidence: antler.co/apply serves a live application form that accepts input: first name, last name, email, LinkedIn, a stage selector offering "Idea to Pre-Seed - Founding to first traction" and "Series A to C", a region selector including Europe, and a city selector listing "Continental Europe (Amsterdam/Berlin)". The success state reads "APPLICATION RECEIVED! Thanks! Your application is with the Antler team." No closed notice anywhere.
programmes.cohort_dates: Residency runs twice a year, starting March and September. Antler also states it invites teams with early traction into its offices year-round, outside residency dates, and writes cheques in a few weeks.
programmes.cash: Up to 500,000 EUR first commitment, and 30M EUR or more through Series C
programmes.terms_dilution: Equity investment; the percentage is not published on the page
programmes.credits_and_tools: 650,000 EUR or more in credits for AI, software and cloud; the location page also cites 4M EUR or more in credits
programmes.customer_access: Antler Expand programme for international growth
programmes.network_quality: Very high - a cohort of around 100 hand-picked founders selected from roughly 10,000 applicants
programmes.location_requirement: In person. Complete teams join for around six weeks; teams based in Munich or Amsterdam typically join the community physically in Berlin for two weeks first. Applicants must meet visa eligibility requirements for their chosen residency location.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Explicitly welcomes solo founders: solo founders or incomplete teams join for around ten weeks, using the early phase to shape direction and founder dynamics while continuing to build. The location page also notes some founders show up solo and pre-idea.
programmes.application_effort: Roughly 30 to 60 minutes; a short form plus an optional pitch deck upload with a 10MB limit. No video required.
programmes.notes: Best structural fit in DACH: rolling, solo-friendly, pre-incorporation, real money, and an explicit year-round door for teams with momentum outside the residency dates - which is the door a working product should knock on rather than the co-founder-matching track. The portfolio skews B2B software: Netbird, simplyblock, LangWatch. The German visa is the open question and the page names it as a requirement, not a formality.

programmes.name: EWOR Fellowship (Traction and Ideation)
programmes.page_evidence: ewor.com/faq: "We review applications and accept fellows on a rolling basis", with responses expected within three weeks. The apply page loads and serves the fellowship application entry. One caveat worth flagging: ewor.com/apply also renders a countdown headed "EWOR Fellowship Applications close in" whose digits did not resolve in the fetched text, so a hard cut-off may coexist with the rolling language.
programmes.cohort_dates: Virtual-first and decentralised; no fixed cohort dates
programmes.cash: Traction Fellowship: 500,000 EUR guaranteed, comprising 110,000 EUR from EWOR GmbH and 390,000 EUR from the fund via an uncapped convertible note or similar. Ideation Fellowship: up to 300,000 EUR.
programmes.terms_dilution: Traction: the FAQ states there is no tuition fee for the Traction Fellowship. Ideation: if EWOR invests it receives 3% of the equity as a tuition fee.
programmes.credits_and_tools: null
programmes.network_quality: Very high on paper - mentors are unicorn founders, and roughly 35 fellows are accepted from more than 35,000 applicants a year
programmes.location_requirement: None. The fellowship is described as virtual-first, decentralised and borderless, reflecting a founder who might build a product in Nairobi, hire in Europe and fundraise in Silicon Valley.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Explicitly accommodates solo applicants: the FAQ tells applicants to choose one person to apply, preferably the CEO or CTO, and list any other co-founders
programmes.application_effort: The FAQ states applicants typically take 15 to 20 minutes to complete the form - unusually light for the size of the cheque
programmes.notes: The single best-matched programme found in this lane. It clears every one of the founder's structural constraints at once: no entity needed (if you have not incorporated, EWOR asks you to do so within 18 months), no relocation, solo accepted, rolling review. The Traction track is the one to target, and it turns on what counts as traction - EWOR's own framing is revenue, active users, pilot projects, initial patents or built hardware, alongside the line that whether you make 500k ARR or do not yet have an idea does not matter because they invest in people. A shipped 5,172-commit product with zero users is an awkward but arguable Traction case and a safe Ideation case. Acceptance rate is roughly 0.1%.

programmes.name: Venture Kick
programmes.organisation: Venture Kick, a Swiss private and philanthropic initiative
programmes.page_evidence: venturekick.ch/getthekick: "We are taking applications at any time!" - a live rolling invitation with links to conditions of participation, a confidentiality agreement and an FAQ. No closed notice.

programmes.cash: Up to CHF 150,000 staged as CHF 10,000, then CHF 40,000, then CHF 100,000. Stage 2 winners qualify to apply for a CHF 150,000 InnoBooster grant; Stage 3 unlocks access to up to CHF 850,000 from Kickfund.
programmes.terms_dilution: The first CHF 10,000 is a non-repayable grant with a moral pledge to repay on success. The CHF 40,000 and CHF 100,000 tranches are convertible loans converting at the next significant equity round.

programmes.network_quality: High in Switzerland

A TUM affiliation does not satisfy this. Separately the project must be pre-commercial with no employees and no commercial revenues, and founders must apply before company incorporation.
programmes.notes: The Swiss-academic-affiliation test is the wall, and it is a genuine eligibility rule rather than a preference. The one theoretical route through it - the "or collaborate with one" clause - would require manufacturing a real research collaboration with a Swiss institution, which is not a same-month move.

programmes.network_quality: High in Italy - reported that 80% of graduates receive investment with an average cheque of 300,000 EUR
programmes.location_requirement: Rome or Milan
programmes.notes: The strongest generalist digital accelerator in Italy and the most plausible Italian door for a B2B SaaS product, since the CDP network is almost entirely vertical. Both known application URLs are dead, so phase 2 needs to find the live one starting from lventuregroup.com directly.

programmes.name: CyberXcelerator (CDP National Accelerators Network)
programmes.organisation: CDP Venture Capital, managed by Startup Wise Guys, with Leonardo, Italgas, NTT Data and Universita della Calabria
programmes.page_evidence: The CDP fund page describes the mechanism - "Interested start-ups can apply through the website of the accelerator, which... launches a call for applications each year" - but does not itself state whether any individual accelerator's call is open. The CyberXcelerator programme site was not reached in this pass.
programmes.cohort_dates: Programmes run 3 to 4 batches, each accelerating around 8 to 10 startups
programmes.cash: Initial pre-seed investment of 70,000 to 200,000 EUR, with possible follow-on seed of 200,000 to 500,000 EUR. The fund can later invest directly in Series A/B at 1M to 5M EUR.
programmes.terms_dilution: Equity, via investment vehicles created for each programme
programmes.credits_and_tools: null
programmes.customer_access: Leonardo as main partner, Italgas as corporate partner, NTT Data as technology partner
programmes.network_quality: Medium to high in Italy
programmes.location_requirement: Based at NTT Data's offices in Cosenza. CDP states its programmes are open to Italian startups and to international ventures looking to open a branch in Italy.
programmes.notes: This is the only one of CDP's 20 vertical accelerators whose focus - CyberTech and AI - could plausibly admit an AI product-lifecycle system, and even then the cyber framing is a stretch. The genuinely useful fact from the CDP fund page is the branch rule: international ventures are eligible if willing to open an Italian operating branch, which for this founder is a lighter ask than an Indian entity. The other nineteen verticals - food, fashion, tourism, proptech, aerospace, blue economy, silver economy, welfare, mobility, cleantech, bioeconomy, digital manufacturing, 5G and IoT, fintech, edtech, health, infratech, sport, and AI-web3-metaverse - are all sector-excluded or too narrow.

programmes.name: PoliHub acceleration and Call4Startups
programmes.organisation: PoliHub, the innovation centre of Politecnico di Milano
programmes.page_evidence: The programmes index tags several calls explicitly as Closed (Encubator, DeepTech Alliance Health 2025, ESA BIC Milan) and leaves others untagged, but shows no open or closed statement for the core acceleration programme itself and no current deadline. A secondary source says you can apply at any time, which the site does not confirm.
programmes.cohort_dates: 12 to 16 week acceleration programme
programmes.cash: null
programmes.credits_and_tools: Mentorship, personalised meetings, business strategy and pitching assistance
programmes.network_quality: High in Italy
programmes.location_requirement: Milan
programmes.notes: The visible calls skew climate, health, space and student-facing (Switch2Product, TechFormers, Basilicata Open LAB, ESA BIC Milan). No obvious slot for a B2B AI product-lifecycle platform, but PoliHub does reportedly accept rolling incubation applications outside named calls, which is the route to test.

programmes.name: Nana Bianca
programmes.page_evidence: Only the homepage description was seen via search results - acceleration programs, coworking spaces and events to support the growth of startups in Italy. No application page, deadline or open/closed statement was reached.
programmes.cohort_dates: null
programmes.cash: null
programmes.credits_and_tools: Coworking space in Florence, plus a startup studio
programmes.network_quality: Medium in Italy
programmes.location_requirement: Florence
programmes.notes: Included for lane coverage of Italian startup studios. Low signal; verify only if the higher-value Italian doors such as LUISS EnLabs turn out to be closed.

programmes.name: Web Summit ALPHA startup programme
programmes.page_evidence: websummit.com/startups serves a live application form with a business email field and "Apply now" and "Apply for 2026" controls, plus a "What happens when I apply?" flow: chat to our specialist team, assessment and selection, prepare with our startup success team, time for Web Summit. No closed notice.
programmes.cohort_dates: Web Summit 2026 runs 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-12 at the Altice Arena and FIL in Lisbon
programmes.cash: None
programmes.terms_dilution: None; this is a paid ticket package
programmes.credits_and_tools: null
programmes.customer_access: Investor-to-startup meetings, a one-day exhibition booth, and a startup profile visible to attendees, investors, media and partners
programmes.network_quality: Very high by volume, shallow by depth - this is a conference, not a cohort
programmes.brand_value: Medium - recognisable, but not selective in the way an accelerator is
programmes.location_requirement: Lisbon for four days in November
programmes.application_effort: Roughly 30 minutes; an email-first form followed by a conversation with the startup team
programmes.notes: A different animal from the rest of this list: ALPHA buys exposure, not capital and not a programme. Selected ALPHA startups get three tickets, a one-day booth, a printed exhibition board, app access, Startup Lounge access, PITCH and Mentor Hours access, and a dedicated startup success manager. Relevant mainly as a launch venue - the mid-September public launch lands seven weeks before the event.

programmes.name: Road 2 Web Summit
programmes.organisation: Startup Portugal and Web Summit, supported by Galp
programmes.page_evidence: startupportugal.com/programs/road-2-web-summit: "Pre-register now. Applications will open soon - pre-register today and be among the first startups notified when applications go live."
programmes.cohort_dates: Preparation programme ahead of Web Summit, 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-12
programmes.cash: None; one Most Promising Startup award
programmes.credits_and_tools: Preparation sessions and exclusive resources
programmes.network_quality: Medium - ecosystem leaders and mentors within Portugal
programmes.location_requirement: Portugal
programmes.hard_blocker: Scoped to Portugal's most promising early-stage startups and gated behind Portuguese Startup Recognition status, which requires a Portuguese entity.
programmes.notes: Recorded to close out the Portuguese branch of the lane. Not reachable without a Portuguese entity. The parent programme, Web Summit ALPHA, is the reachable version of the same opportunity.

programmes.name: Unicorn Factory Lisboa (Incubation and Scaling Up)
programmes.organisation: Unicorn Factory Lisboa and Startup Lisboa, an initiative of the City of Lisbon
programmes.page_evidence: The homepage describes incubation, acceleration and scaleup programmes and carries a "Join Us" control, but states no application status, no deadline and no cohort dates for any individual programme.
programmes.cohort_dates: Scaling Up is on its ninth edition, having reached 78 growth-phase companies
programmes.cash: null
programmes.credits_and_tools: Vertical innovation hubs and coworking
programmes.network_quality: Medium to high in Portugal - 1,100+ startups supported, 1bn EUR or more fundraised across the portfolio
programmes.location_requirement: Lisbon
programmes.application_effort: Application plus acceptance at a Jury Session for the acceleration programme
programmes.notes: Scaling Up is explicitly for companies in the growth and internationalisation phase, which is above Supaprod's stage. The Incubation programme, run via Startup Lisboa, is the stage-appropriate one. Also relevant as one of the certified incubators that can sponsor a Portugal Startup Visa.

programmes.name: Portugal Startup Visa
programmes.organisation: IAPMEI, the Portuguese Agency for Competitiveness and Innovation, via a certified incubator
programmes.page_evidence: No IAPMEI or Startup Portugal page stating the current application status was fetched in this pass; all detail came from immigration-advisory secondary sources rather than the scheme's own page.
programmes.cohort_dates: Rolling; processing reported at 6 to 11 months
programmes.cash: None. The applicant must show roughly 5,146.80 EUR per year in living expenses.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Incubation by the sponsoring certified incubator
programmes.customer_access: Depends entirely on which of the 99 certified incubators sponsors the applicant
programmes.network_quality: Varies by sponsoring incubator
programmes.brand_value: Low as a credential, high as an option
programmes.location_requirement: Portugal. Grants two years of residency, a path to permanent residence, and citizenship eligibility after five years.
programmes.application_effort: A viable and innovative business plan approved by a certified incubator, then an IAPMEI submission, then the visa application itself
programmes.notes: Not an accelerator and it will never be a credential on a deck. It is on this list because it is the cheapest legal route in the whole lane for a non-EU solo founder to acquire an EU base: incubator approval first, then IAPMEI, then residency. Relevant only if the founder decides an EU base is strategically worth having; irrelevant otherwise.
